cards.title: Interlaboratory Variability in Hepatocyte CLint
cards.claim: In vitro CLint values for the same compound can vary significantly across laboratories (CVs up to 99.8%), and this variability is not dependent on the number of published values (n). This variability propagates into IVIVE predictions, often resulting in systematic underprediction for high-clearance compounds.
conditions: Variability is driven by experimental procedure differences (e.g., shaking intensity) rather than just donor variability.
High permeability compounds (low rotatable bonds) are more susceptible to this variability due to unstirred water layer (UWL) effects.
required_inputs: Multiple published CLint values for the same compound from different sources.
Physicochemical properties (logD, rotatable bonds, protein binding).
limitations: Retrospective analysis of existing literature; does not provide a universal correction factor.
Does not account for all potential sources of experimental error.
Findings are specific to the dataset of 50 compounds analyzed.
cards.downstream_use: Use this to justify caution when selecting in vitro data for IVIVE. If multiple CLint values exist, assess their consistency. If variability is high, consider the impact on predicted hepatic clearance (CLH) and acknowledge uncertainty in human simulations.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
